findings.description: AWS access key and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the EC2 user_data script, which is retrievable via the instance metadata service, EC2 describe-instance-attribute API calls, and Terraform state, risking credential compromise.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, leaving data stored on the volume unencrypted at rest.

The EBS snapshot inherits encryption status from the unencrypted source volume, meaning the snapshot itself is stored unencrypted, exposing data at rest, including in any copies or cross-account shares.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the administrative management interface of the instance to the entire internet.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0. While plausible for a public web server, combined with the public subnet, public IP assignment, and open SSH rule with no compensating network layering, this widens the overall attack surface.
The security group allows all outbound traffic to any destination (0.0.0.0/0, all ports/protocols), which increases the risk of data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet, especially combined with the open security group.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IPs to instances launched in this subnet, increasing exposure to the internet.
The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving potentially sensitive network log data unencrypted at rest.
The S3 bucket has no public access block, bucket policy, or ACL restrictions defined, risking unintended public exposure of flow log data.
